agent_vs_you: The agent made four independent qwen generations and its prompts dropped most of the user's spec: no 'sage-green-and-cream' palette, no pot, no paper texture, no border or lettering description. It relied on the words 'same border style' and 'simple consistent layout', which mean nothing to four separate generations that never see each other. The style guard then prefixed a garbled capture of the user's sentence ('In a linocut style throughout: same border style:'). Each slide invented its own border, font, ink colour (three black, one green) and none drew a pot. For a carousel that must share an exact template I would design slide 1 with every shared element spelled out, then make slides 2-4 as edits of slide 1 that swap only the plant and the name. An edit carries the border, paper, pot and lettering over; a new generation does not.

your_plan.say: I'll design the Monstera slide first with the full sage-green-and-cream linocut template (border, paper, pot, lettering), then make the other three as edits of that slide that change only the plant and its name, so all four match.

A thick hand-carved sage-green linocut border with small notched corners frames the slide. Centred: a monstera plant with large split leaves growing from a simple rounded pot with a thick rim, plant and pot carved in sage green with cream highlights. Below the pot, the single word "Monstera" in bold, slightly rough linocut-style serif lettering in sage green, centred. No other text.

fix: 1) Planner rule and catalogue CHOOSING line: 'A SET THAT SHARES ONE DESIGN (carousel, series, menu cards, event pack): make the first piece with every shared element spelled out (palette, border, lettering, paper, recurring objects), then each other piece as an image-edit OF THE FIRST that changes only the variable part (parallel, from the same master); never N independent generations.' 2) Add to image POORLY: 'the same border, font or layout across separate generations'. 3) Harness style guard: stop the capture at ':' as well as ',;.', keep the user's colour words with the style ('sage-green-and-cream linocut'), and do not prefix when the prompt already leads with the style. 4) A pre-run check: every colour word and named object in the sheet's quotes must appear in each image prompt (the palette and the pot were dropped).
evidence: The four 640x640 slides are spelled correctly and in order, and the plants are recognisable. But 01_monstera has a patterned black border, black ink and sans lettering; 02_snake_plant a rough black frame, black ink and sans lettering; 03_pothos no border, green watercolour-like foliage and serif lettering; 04_peace_lily a double-line frame, black ink and serif lettering.
